powers.name: The Kingdom of Deepmark

contingents.what: stone-guard of the deep halls
deep-miners

holds.name: the stair-gate in the Given Land's bedrock

powers.wantsFromYou: The truth, weighed. Deepmark deals only with people who say what they mean.
powers.offersYou: Stone that will bear any weight, and a king's honest measure.
powers.leverage: Odran cannot abide a lie, even a kind one, and will break a deal over it.
powers.whenBroken: The stair-gate closes, and the Masons above feel their floor go hollow.
powers.plainly: An underground dwarven kingdom in the deep stone beneath the Given Land, ruled by a king who trusts only what has never been above ground.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Masons of the Given Land believe only what can be touched. The dwarves under them went further: they believe only what has never been touched by daylight. Deepmark's king measures every word as he would a block of stone, and lately the deepest shaft has started to ring.
powers.appearance: A stair cut into bedrock that does not stop, halls of black stone lit by forge-glow, and a throne carved from the floor

boatmen and cavern-farmers

holds.name: the double-locked door at the top of the stair

powers.wantsFromYou: To be watched the whole time you are here, and to accept it.
powers.offersYou: The only safe trade route between the Descent and everyone else.
powers.leverage: The Queen fears the Descent more than she shows; an ally against it would be worth anything.
powers.whenBroken: The lower door opens and the Bargain Gate's traders walk up the stair unwatched.
powers.plainly: A dwarven kingdom around an underground lake in the caverns beside the Descent, trading with the Abyssal Choir and keeping its doors locked from both sides.
powers.descriptionSeed: Undermere sits between the world and the Descent and makes its living from that. Lake-Queen Sigrun trades with the Abyssal Choir and with everyone else, and keeps a lock on each face of her door, because she knows what the Choir sells and how it is paid for.
powers.appearance: A black lake under a cavern roof, stone quays, lamplit boats, a city in tiers round the water, and a great door with a lock on each face

foragers and wood-tenders

powers.offersYou: Safe passage through the deep forest, and healing no one outside it can do.
powers.leverage: The Evenwood will do much to keep the ents' agreement private.
powers.whenBroken: The lanterns go out in the high trees and the forest closes over the paths.
powers.plainly: An elven forest territory where the great western forest meets the Deepwood. The elves and the ents are the two oldest things in it.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Evenwood's elves have shared the deep forest with the ents for longer than either people has been counting, under an agreement about which of them is older that neither will say aloud. canopy-walkers and silverwood cutters

powers.offersYou: Silverwood, elven bows, and a view of the world from above the trees.
powers.leverage: The Silverbough cannot bear to be seen. Whoever can show them to the world below has their attention.
powers.whenBroken: The halls go dark and the rope-stair hangs down for anyone, which is worse.
powers.plainly: Elven halls built into the high canopy of the southern forest. You can walk a day beneath it and not know it is there.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Silverbough is a city nobody below has seen, and its lord intends to keep it that way. Greyspire's dwarves can see its lanterns from their walls, and the two holds have argued and traded across the tree-line for four centuries; lately the rope-stair has been drawn up.
powers.appearance: Silver-barked trees with halls and bridges in the canopy, lantern-light seen from below as a silver haze, and a rope-stair let down only for guests

tenders of the floating gardens

powers.offersYou: The view from above everything, and elven learning no one below can match.
powers.leverage: The city is sinking. Whoever can help the Archon without being told why has her favour.
powers.whenBroken: The stair comes down for the last time, and the city drifts away over the Pattern Reach and is not seen again.
powers.plainly: An elven sky city drifting above the high ground at the Pattern Reach's edge. The Figurists say it is held up by an idea.
powers.descriptionSeed: Highmere floats, and nobody below understands why. The Figurists say it is held up by an idea; the elves say that is the same thing, and the Archon lets them argue. This year the city has dropped twenty feet, and the Archon has ordered that no one mention it.
powers.appearance: White towers on a floating island of rock, waterfalls turning to cloud before they land, and a long pale stair that reaches the ground only when Highmere wants it to

powers.leverage: The chains are everything. Whoever threatens them, or guards them, has the Windlord's whole attention.

powers.plainly: An elven sky city anchored to the eastern peaks by chains a mile long. Its people come down to trade and to fight at the Crossing.

reef-gardeners

powers.offersYou: Safe passage on the Inner Sea, pearls, and merfolk healing.
powers.leverage: The Queen wants a seat among the Mavens that does not have to be carried in. Help with that is remembered.
powers.whenBroken: The reef city goes dark and the Inner Sea's ships start to founder where they never did.
powers.plainly: A merfolk court in the reefs of the Inner Sea. Its envoys come ashore at Thinwater on the full tide; the Mavens keep a pool in the Crossing for them.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Coral Court is the largest people of the Inner Sea, and the gentlest, until the sea is threatened. Queen Marisol meets land-folk in a ring of stones at the tide-line, and this year the reef nearest Thinwater has begun to die.

fishers and salters

powers.leverage: The Netguild sells to everyone; whoever would make them choose a side makes an enemy of the whole town.

powers.plainly: A stilt-town over the shallows of the western sea: salt-pans, net-lofts, boats for streets. It sells to anyone.

contingents.what: leviathan-riders
outriders and harness-tenders

holds.name: the harness-camp on the lead leviathan's back

powers.wantsFromYou: To leave the leviathans unhunted. That is the whole of it.
powers.offersYou: Passage across the ocean at the speed of a leviathan, and riders who fight like nothing else alive.
powers.leverage: Anyone who harms a leviathan has the whole Road as an enemy; anyone who saves one has it as a friend.
powers.whenBroken: The riders scatter, and the leviathans are hunted on every coast within a generation.
powers.plainly: The riders who follow the great leviathans across the world ocean, living on the backs of beasts the size of towns.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Leviathan Road is a migration and a people. The riders live on the leviathans' backs and come ashore only to trade and to fight, and they have one law: nobody hunts a leviathan. This season, for the first time in living memory, the leviathans have turned north.
powers.appearance: A line of vast backs breaking the ocean surface, huts and harness-rigging on them, and riders standing on the swell as if it were a road

powers.name: The Sunwardens of Sunfold

contingents.what: Sunwardens who climb the works
cutting-crews and farmers who hold the line against the Long Noon

holds.name: the clock-tower, which strikes the sun's hours

powers.wantsFromYou: Hands at the cut line in the growing season, and anything you know about how a kept sun works.
powers.offersYou: Grain, bread, and a bed under a sun, which is worth more than it sounds two strata down.
powers.leverage: Half the Near Under eats Sunfold's grain. Whoever threatens the sun threatens all of them, and the Sunwardens know it.
powers.whenBroken: The fields go untended, the Long Noon crosses the west wall in a season, and the Near Under is hungry by winter.
powers.plainly: The farming town under a kept sun, two strata down, and the order that keeps the sun rising.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Sunwardens keep a machine nobody alive built, so that a town can farm under it. They are farmers first and keepers second, and they are getting better at the second because they have to.
powers.appearance: Sun-browned people in work-clothes with brass keys on chains, climbing ladders into a sun.
powers._sng671: Erik 2026-10-04: 'yes' to the deep places. The ruling power of a kept-sun town.

powers.wantsFromYou: To stay away from the caps, or to help keep them shut.
powers.offersYou: Guides down the old harvest ways, and rain.
powers.leverage: The Enginewrights need the Boreborn to keep the caps and do not trust them; the Boreborn need the Wrights' iron and do not trust them back.
powers.whenBroken: The caps go unwatched. Nobody knows what that means, which is the reason they were watched.
powers.plainly: The descendants of the harvest crews, who live in a vault with its own weather and keep the caps on the old bores.
powers.descriptionSeed: The Boreborn's ancestors drew the core up those shafts. The Boreborn keep them shut, and are not sure whether that is penance, duty, or fear.
powers.appearance: Weathered people in oilskins with harvest tattoos on their arms, ringing iron caps with hammers and listening.
powers._sng671: Erik 2026-10-04: 'yes' to the deep places. The keepers of the caps.
